# Uptime Monitor - product brief

## Problem

Small teams running a handful of internal services need to know when one of them goes down. Existing paid tools are overkill for a fleet of ten to twenty checks and existing self-hosted options need weekly attention to stay running.

## Users

- The single operator who owns the fleet and its uptime.
- The occasional teammate who wants to glance at status without a login they need to remember.

## Must-haves (v1)

1. HTTP monitor: given a URL and an expected status, poll on a schedule, record pass and fail with timestamps.
2. Read-only dashboard: shows every monitor's current status and the last twenty-four hours of results.
3. Signed-in admin surface: add, edit and remove monitors; runs on the same web app under an authenticated route.
4. Outbound recovery emails via Resend when a monitor moves from failing back to passing.

## Should-haves (v1)

- Alert email on the first fail after a passing run.
- CSV export of a monitor's last thirty days.

## Non-functional constraints

- Runs on a single Node process, less than one hundred megabytes resident.
- Handles two hundred monitors on a one-minute poll without falling behind.

## Out of scope for v1

- Slack, SMS, or webhook notifications.
- Multi-tenant sign-in; one operator per install.
- Read-only dashboard authentication; the read view is anonymous by design.
